thread.title: Arista shares plunge as Cisco fight resurfaces in earnings, Silicon Valley stocks dip

author: Marlize van Romburgh
title: Arista shares plunge as Cisco fight resurfaces in earnings, Silicon Valley stocks dip
text: – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 16, 2018, 1:50pm PST Arista Networks shares plummeted 19 percent on Friday, despite beating earnings and guidance expectations, as it said that it’s ongoing battle with archival Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO) hurt sales. Arista's (NYSE: ANET) fourth-quarter revenue rose 43 percent to $467.9 million, beating analyst expectations of $463 million. Earnings per share came in at $1.71, beating analysts' predictions of $1.42. The Santa Clara-based company is forecasting current quarter revenue of $450 million to $468 million, compared to an average analyst estimate of $457 million. But, according to Investor's Business Daily , executives said on an earnings call with analysts that revenue growth from its cloud customers, which include Facebook (NASDAQ: FB), Amazon.com (NASDAQ: AMZN) and Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ: MSFT), slowed. The company apparently pinned the slump on a “workaround” tied to its ongoing patent infringement fight with San Jose-based Cisco. Arista was founded in 2004 by former Cisco executives. CEO Jayshree Ullal , another former leader at Cisco, joined the company in 2008 and helped take it public in 2014. Friday’s sell-off was the highest volume of trading ever for the company's shares, Investor’s Business Daily noted. Meanwhile, Cisco reported blockbuster earnings this week and its stock soared to a 17-year high on Thursday . Among all Silicon Valley stocks, those that posted the biggest gains on Friday: Roku (NASDAQ: ROKU) powered up 5.46 percent. SunPower (NASDAQ: SPWR) surged 3.38 percent. Viavi Solutions (NASDAQ: VIAV) gained 2.37 percent. Infinera Corp. (NASDAQ: INFN) bounced 2.29 percent. Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT) closed up 1.93 percent. The biggest decliners, after Arista, were: Coherent (NASDAQ: COHR), slipped 4.07 percent. Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) fell 3.04 percent. Mellanox Technologies (NASDAQ: MLNX) slumped 2.6 percent. Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ: SMCI) dipped 2.05 percent. The Bloomberg Silicon Valley High Tech Index dipped 0.3 percent on Friday, as seven of the 13 stocks on the index fell. The worst performers were AMD, Juniper Networks (NYSE: JNPR), Facebook and Intel Corp. (NASDAQ: INTC) The only stocks on the index that closed up were Applied Materials, eBay (NASDAQ: EBAY), Cisco, Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) and Oracle Corp. (NASDAQ: ORCL). Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), the biggest stock in the region, slipped 0.32 percent.
